questions.q: In 'The Dog and His Reflection', what did the Dog think he saw in the water?
choices: Another Dog with a bigger bone
A fish swimming under the plank
A cat sitting on the far bank
The butcher looking for his meat
questions.evidence: a real Dog carrying a bone much bigger than his own

questions.q: What is the lesson of 'The Dog and His Reflection'?
choices: It is very foolish to be greedy
Always look before you jump in
Dogs cannot swim with a bone
Bridges are very dangerous
questions.evidence: It is very foolish to be greedy.

questions.q: In 'The Hare and the Tortoise', why did the Hare lie down for a nap during the race?
choices: To show how silly it was to race a Hare
Because he felt sick from running so fast
Because the Fox told him it was allowed
Because it was getting dark and late
questions.evidence: he lay down beside the course to take a nap

questions.q: In 'The Hare and the Tortoise', what happened while the Hare was sleeping?
choices: The Tortoise passed him
The Fox ended the race
The Tortoise gave up
It began to rain hard
questions.evidence: passed the place where the Hare was sleeping

questions.q: What is the lesson of 'The Hare and the Tortoise'?
choices: The race is not always to the swift
Never take a nap in the afternoon
Foxes are always fair and wise judges
Tortoises are much faster than hares
questions.evidence: The race is not always to the swift.

questions.q: In 'The Bees and Wasps, and the Hornet', how did the wise old Bee say to settle the case?
choices: Have both sides build a honey comb
Split all the honey right in half
Let the Ant decide who owns it
Have a race to the top of the tree

questions.q: In 'The Bees and Wasps, and the Hornet', why did the Wasps protest loudly?
choices: They knew they could not build a comb and fill it
They wanted much more time to think about the case
They did not like the Ant and did not trust her
They were afraid of what the Hornet would decide
questions.evidence: They knew they could not build a honey comb and fill it with honey.

questions.q: In 'The Lark and Her Young Ones', why did the Mother Lark decide to leave at last?
choices: The Farmer said he and his son would do the work
The heavy ripe wheat fell down on top of the nest
The neighbors had finally arrived to cut the field
The young Larks were hungry and could not wait
questions.evidence: Tomorrow we must set to work, ourselves.
